articles.title: How to retrieve a Scalekit client secret
articles.content: To retrieve your client secret in Scalekit, log in to the Scalekit Admin Dashboard, select your environment (e.g., Development or Production), navigate to 'API Settings' or 'Client Credentials', and click 'Generate Secret'. Make sure to copy it immediately, as it will only be displayed once.

articles.title: OAuth Redirect URI Setup Guide
articles.content: When setting up Single Sign-On (SSO) or OAuth, you must configure a Redirect URI. The redirect URI is where the authorization server sends the user after successful authentication. For local testing, use: http://localhost:5000/auth/callback. In production, ensure this is set to your HTTPS backend endpoint and matches exactly.

articles.title: LangGraph Agent Troubleshooting Guidelines
articles.content: If the LangGraph support agent fails with status 422 (sources are empty or not allowed), check if a web search was performed via Tavily. The agent's response format schema requires that any source URL returned must be a subset of the Tavily search results. If the user explicitly asks for docs or oauth features, the web search will trigger, so ensure TAVILY_API_KEY is active.

articles.title: Resolving Webhook Signature Failures
articles.content: Webhook verification errors usually happen when the payload is modified or parsed before hashing. Verify that: 1. You are using the raw request body buffer to compute the HMAC-SHA256 signature. 2. The signing secret matches the secret from your developer portal. 3. The signature algorithm is SHA-256.

[AGENT RESPONSE] Hi support team, I'm setting up SSO authentication with Scalekit in our React app, but when the user logs in, I keep getting a redirect_uri_mismatch error at http://localhost:5000/auth/callback. How do I configure the authorized redirect URIs?

Hello,

Thank you for reaching out. The "redirect_uri_mismatch" error typically occurs when the redirect URI sent by your application does not exactly match the one registered in your Scalekit settings.

To resolve this, please log in to your Scalekit Admin Dashboard and navigate to Authentication > Redirects > Allowed Callback URLs. Ensure that 'http://localhost:5000/auth/callback' is added there exactly as it appears in your application configuration. Note that OAuth providers compare these URIs as literal strings, so they must match character-for-character.

Could you please verify that the URI in your code and the dashboard are identical? If the issue persists after updating these settings, let us know and we can investigate further.

[AGENT RESPONSE] Our production deployment is completely broken. Webhook HMAC-SHA256 signature verification in Node.js Express is constantly failing with crypto.timingSafeEqual returning false. We verified the signing secret 5 times. This is blocking our entire customer rollout!

Hello, thank you for reaching out. We understand the urgency of this issue, especially as it is impacting your production rollout.

In Node.js Express environments, HMAC signature verification failures most frequently occur because the request body is being parsed as JSON before the signature is verified. To ensure a successful match, you must use the raw request body buffer. If you are using standard middleware, you may need to configure `express.raw()` or use a custom verify function to capture the raw body buffer before it is processed.

Additionally, please confirm that the buffers passed to `crypto.timingSafeEqual` are of the same byte length, as a mismatch will cause verification to fail immediately. Could you please share the part of your code where the request body is captured and the signature is computed? This will help us investigate further.

[AGENT RESPONSE] We are getting a critical webhook signature verification failure in Node.js Express. crypto.timingSafeEqual returns false on all incoming Stripe webhook events. How do we access the raw body buffer to compute the HMAC-SHA256 signature?

Hello, thank you for reaching out to our support team.

Webhook signature verification failures in Node.js Express environments typically occur when the request body is parsed into a JSON object before the signature is verified. To resolve this, you must ensure you are using the raw, unparsed request body buffer for the HMAC-SHA256 calculation.

If you are using middleware like `express.json()`, please verify that it is defined after your webhook route. If it is applied globally before the route, it will modify the payload and cause the signature check to fail. 

Could you please confirm your current middleware configuration and if you are using the `stripe-node` library? This will help us provide more specific guidance.

Once you are in the correct environment, navigate to the 'API Settings' or 'Client Credentials' section and click 'Generate Secret'. Please ensure you copy the secret immediately, as it is only displayed once for security purposes. 

If you encounter any issues during this process, please let us know.

Hello, thank you for reaching out. Webhook signature verification failures in Node.js Express are commonly caused by the request body being parsed into a JSON object before the signature is verified. 

To resolve this, you must use the raw request body buffer for the HMAC-SHA256 computation. In Express, this typically requires ensuring that middleware like `express.json()` is not applied to the webhook route, or using a custom `verify` function within the middleware to capture the raw buffer before it is processed.
